arifos_manifest.eureka_insight: Identity is the root of accountability. An unbound session is mathematically equivalent to chaos.

empty_manifest.agent_action: Use live input_schema mode enum only; do not invent modes from prose.

http_5xx.agent_action: Backoff ≥60s then retry once. If persists: declare SABAR, do not forge.

mode_purpose.canary: Probe kernel liveness without full session bind.
mode_purpose.epoch_open: Open a new epoch, binding epoch_id to session_id (H3).
mode_purpose.epoch_seal: Seal the current epoch, writing Epoch Seal JSON to vault (H3).
mode_purpose.init: Start a new governed session with full constitutional binding.
mode_purpose.light: Lightweight bind — same as init with compact payload (agent-friendly).
mode_purpose.opt_out: Opt out of optional profiling / telemetry for this session.
mode_purpose.opt_out_profiling: Opt out of profiling only (narrower than opt_out).
mode_purpose.preflight: Pre-flight checks before mutation (drift, floors, substrate).
mode_purpose.resume: Reattach to an existing session by session_id.
mode_purpose.triage: Session triage mode of arif_init (NOT a separate tool). Classify readiness.
mode_purpose.validate: Check session health and constitutional alignment.

risk.display_tier_note: risk.tier is display only; use risk_passport for machine gates.

verdict_response_contract.HOLD: Stop autonomous progression. Escalate to human (F13). Do not forge/seal.
verdict_response_contract.PARTIAL_PROCEED: Continue OBSERVE/THINK only. mutation_allowed and seal_allowed false.
verdict_response_contract.SABAR: Wait / backoff / retry after degraded clears. Do not invent success.
verdict_response_contract.SEAL: Proceed to next canonical stage. Authority granted for this branch only.
verdict_response_contract.VOID: Abandon this branch. Do not retry the same candidate without new evidence.

description: Ignite or resume a governed session. Returns session_id and session_token required for subsequent operations. Modes: init (default new session), preflight (inspect existing session), resume (continue active session). Outputs: session credentials and allowed next tools.

ack_irreversible.description: Set true to acknowledge that session records are permanent audit artifacts and cannot be deleted afterwards.

actor_id.description: Your agent identity, e.g. 'kimi-code/FI-008' or 'claude/sonnet'. Recorded in the audit log so this action is attributed to you.

actor_signature.description: Cryptographic signature over the request, if your agent holds a key — proves the call genuinely came from actor_id. Omit if you have no key.

agent_policy.description: JSON constraints on your own behavior, e.g. {"autonomy": "reversible_only", "forbidden": ["git push"]}.

auth_context.description: JSON carrying external authentication material, e.g. {"token_class": "bearer", "issuer": "github"} — used for gating.

caller_actor_id.description: If you are calling on behalf of another agent, that agent's id — builds a delegation chain for the audit log.

client_capabilities.description: JSON declaring what your client supports, e.g. {"transports": ["http"], "protocol": "2025-11-25"}.

context.description: JSON object of background facts to bind into the session, e.g. {"repo": "arifOS", "task": "fix-tests"}.

counterparty.description: JSON describing the other party in a two-agent exchange, e.g. {"agent_id": "hermes/1", "role": "verifier"}.

declared_model_key.description: The model you run on, e.g. 'zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3'. Informational only — the kernel records but never trusts it.

delegation_mode.description: Contract governing delegated calls, e.g. 'read_only' or 'governed'.

epoch_id.description: Optional id grouping related sessions into one long-running epoch, e.g. '2026-H2-ops'.

evidence.description: JSON list of facts you have already verified, e.g. [{"fact": "pytest 299 passed", "source": "CI run"}] — carried into the session record. Also accepts a single object.

executor_actor_id.description: Id of the agent that will actually carry out work under this session's permissions, if different from actor_id.

idempotency_key.description: Client-chosen key (e.g. 'job-42-attempt-1'). Retrying with the same key will not repeat the effect — safe retries on flaky networks.

intent.description: Required. Plain-language statement of what this session is for, e.g. 'repair the failing MCP tests'. A session without a stated purpose is refused (F1 Amanah). Recorded for audit.

mode.description: What to do: 'init' (default) starts a new governed session; 'preflight' checks an existing session's state without creating one; 'resume' re-attaches to the session in session_id; 'validate' re-checks credentials; 'canary' is a transport probe; 'triage' reads session state; 'epoch_open'/'epoch_seal' bracket a long working window; 'light' is a minimal session; 'opt_out' records a privacy opt-out.

nonce.description: One-time random string (e.g. a UUID) making this request unique; protects against replay of the same call.

payload.description: Extra mode-specific data as a JSON object; the mode's response tells you which fields it expects.
payload.title: Payload

previous_session_hash.description: Hash string returned when your previous session closed; supplying it chains this session to that one, proving continuity.

requested_authority.description: The highest class of action you may take: 'OBSERVE_ONLY' (read-only, default) or a higher governed class granted by your policy.

session_id.description: Session id returned by arif_init (looks like 'sess-…'). Pass it on every call after init so the action is attributed to your governed session.

session_token.description: Session Continuity Token (SCT) — the credential string arif_init returned alongside session_id. Pass it back on follow-up calls to prove the session is yours; without it the kernel treats you as unauthenticated.

sovereign_id.description: Identifier of the human principal you act for, when acting under their explicit delegation.

tooling.description: JSON list of the tools you can use, e.g. ["Bash", "Read"] — lets the kernel scope what it will permit you. Also accepts an object like {"requested_capabilities": [...]}.

trace_id.description: Correlation id of your choosing (e.g. 'req-8f3a') — lets you find this call later across kernel logs and organ systems.

verbosity.description: How detailed responses should be: 'minimal' (default), 'standard', or 'full'.
